doc.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Trumpet Guild in Holland with the Metropole Orchestra
summary: Pete recalls performing with the Metropole Orchestra and meeting Dokshizer and Maurice Andre.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. Either that or a special deal of some kind or something. And you know now we did, with the Metropole Orchestra, we opened up the Trumpet Guild, I think it was the fifth Trumpet Guild or Brass Trumpet Guild they call it, in Holland. And in there they had trumpet players from South America, Maurice Andre of France that performed with the Philharmonic, and I got to meet Timofei Dokshizer, the great Russian trumpet player. And it was Chuck Findley and Bob Findley, brothers, and Conte and I, we went over there with the Metropole, to rehearse with the Metropole Orchestra, and Rob Pronk, its conductor, and they wrote charts and we talked, corresponded. We did “Doodlin’”, Conte and I did “Doodlin’” and a couple of other things together. He did four of his own and I did four, and the same with the Findleys, Chuck and Bob. And the orchestra, you turned your head and they had a Basie thing in the brasses, it would just scare you. Now it’s backed by the government. No real relation, you understand, but we knew it. And meeting Dokshizer, he called us in Rotterdam the opening night after two weeks they have in Alba. We talked under Dorwin Handy, the interpreter, and he said he loves jazz, loves jazz. I did “Boy Meets Horn” with 85 men you know, things like that, and it turned out wonderful. And he did, I saw a tape of what he did with the Philharmonic, and he and Maurice Andre, he did piccolo trumpet and not just on the trumpet, he has since come here two or three times just the most marvelous guy you ever want to meet in your life. He said, “I was better when I was younger,” he said. And I couldn’t believe that sound. It was unbelievable.
